I'd been going to the same hairdresser for years.
Then she finally moved to a different city, and I had to find someone new.
Honestly, it felt like starting over from scratch.
I found a salon with good reviews online and booked an appointment.
I also brought a photo on my phone, just to be safe.
I figured that would remove any chance of confusion about what I actually wanted.
The stylist looked at the photo for a second and nodded.
She said something like, "Sure, I can do something similar." In hindsight, that probably should have worried me a little more than it did.
She started cutting, and for the first twenty minutes or so, everything seemed pretty normal.
Just small snips here and there.
She kept stepping back to compare my hair to the photo propped up on the counter.
Then she picked up a much bigger section than I expected.
She said something about "adding movement." Before I could really process what that meant, a noticeably large amount of hair was already sitting on the floor beside the chair.
An hour later, I was staring in the mirror at a cut that was, let's just say, only similar in the sense that both involved hair.
Mine was shorter and choppier.
It honestly looked nothing like the soft, layered look in the photo I'd shown her.
I sat there for a second, not really sure what to say.
She spun the chair around proudly, clearly happy with her work, and asked if I loved it as much as she did.
I mean, what do you even say in that moment?
I just sort of smiled, said it was different, and paid.
I didn't know how to explain that "similar" and "identical" apparently meant very different things to her.
I went home and texted a photo to my sister.
She immediately called me, laughing, and said it looked like I'd shown the stylist a completely different picture by accident.
To be fair, that felt about right.
My mom, though, took one look at a photo I sent her and immediately asked if everything was okay.
Honestly, that wasn't the reaction I was hoping for.
But at least it made me laugh instead of panic all over again.
It actually grew on me after a week or two, the way these things sometimes do.
A few people even said they liked the shorter style better than my old one.
So I guess it worked out.
Still, I found a new stylist after that, one who actually asks clarifying questions before touching any scissors.
Now I bring two photos instead of one, just to leave a little less room for creative interpretation.
I also ask, very specifically, how much shorter something will actually end up before any cutting starts.
